description: This course is designed to develop students' Spanish proficiency to mastery level (C1–C2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages, CEFR), refining their interaction, production, reception, and mediation skills through engagement with the cultural production of the Spanish-speaking world. Teaching adopts a seminar-based, collaborative approach, conducted in Spanish, in which students are expected to take an active and analytical role in discussions, readings, and project work. The course is structured around sociocultural units that examine how cinema, photography, graphic novels, and other cultural expressions narrate and bear witness to social change. Units explore themes such as memory and state violence, North–South relations, the ethics of representation, and the experience of minority identities. Through the close analysis of specific cultural objects, students develop the critical and linguistic tools to engage with cultural production as both aesthetic practice and social document. Throughout the academic year, students also undertake an independent research project within a simulated editorial environment, working as cultural journalists for the Cultura section of Enfoques , an online magazine and podcast that promotes understanding of the contexts where Spanish is spoken. Students produce a research dossier for an end-of-year special issue of Enfoques/Cultura . The course thus aims not only to bring students to mastery-level proficiency in Spanish but also to develop their critical engagement with Spanish-speaking contexts, sharpen their research and analytical abilities, and foster sociolinguistic critical awareness.

assessmentText: Exam (30%), duration: 90 minutes in the Spring exam period. Oral examination (30%). Continuous assessment (40%). Language courses map to the Common European Framework for Language Learning. This framework defines linguistic proficiency in the four language skills (reading, writing, speaking and listening) at different levels. To pass this course, students are therefore required to achieve a pass mark in each element of the assessment (continuous assessment, oral and written exams), as these test all four skills.
